messages:
alex: Heads-up — ran long-context (100k token) load tests on the on-prem rig and saw KV cache memory climb to ~60GB, then paging started. Eviction didn't seem to free enough, fragmentation looked high. repro script: `tests/long_ctx/100k_run.sh`

maria_dev: Ugh. Is this on the Dedicated cluster or the Private on-prem box? Any config diffs?

alex: Private on-prem (VPC-offline package). Dedicated runs fine under similar QPS, Hosted also fine. Suspect config drift: private has `kv.paging.enabled=false` historically, but even with paging on, we hit lots of page faults.

chris_sre: Can you paste the profiler output? especially page_faults / free_pages / largest_free_block. Also kernel selection version used on that box?

alex: Pasting the short profiler dump:

```
kv_profiler summary:
  active_entries: 1_024_512
  total_kv_bytes: 57_632_000_000
  page_faults: 13245
  evictions_triggered: 12
  compaction_runs: 0
  frag_ratio: 0.46
  largest_free_block: 12_288_000
```

alex: Kernel runtime: kernel-select v2.3.1 (recent change). Allocator: custom-gpu-alloc v1.2

kv-profiler-bot: auto-report: long_ctx_suite/100k flagged KV memory growth > baseline (baseline 22GB). Regression probability 0.89. Tagging eng-runtime and eng-ml.

maria_dev: frag_ratio 0.46 is pretty bad. On Hosted we compact pages every N evictions; looks like Private disabled compaction for contiguous allocation with older alloc. Did we flip `kv.compact_on_eviction` anywhere?

chris_sre: Confirmed: Dedicated & Hosted default: `kv.paging.enabled=true`, `kv.compact_on_eviction=true`, `kv.page_size=4MB`. Private package had `kv.paging.enabled=false` in /etc/redwood/kv.conf for compatibility with onprem allocator. That explains why compaction_runs=0.

jordan_pm: So why does Dedicated not see the same memory growth? hardware? gpu drivers?

alex: Partly. On-prem box is A100 with older driver; Dedicated uses patched driver and H100 hosts that expose larger contiguous blocks, and our kernel-select picks kernels differently based on GPU. kernel-select v2 puts more emphasis on contiguous KV layouts for faster matmul kernels, which unfortunately increases fragmentation long-term under long sequences.

maria_dev: For immediate mitigation: enable `kv.compact_on_eviction=true` and set `kv.page_threshold=0.75` on the private image. That should force compaction before fragmentation gets too bad. Also reduce `kv.max_free_pages` to avoid keeping many small pockets.

chris_sre: Example config to test (apply with `redwoodctl restart runtime`):

```
kv.paging.enabled=true
kv.compact_on_eviction=true
kv.page_threshold=0.75
kv.page_size=4MB
kv.max_free_pages=64
```

chris_sre: Also, try backporting kernel-select v2.2 heuristics for that node (toggle `kernel-select.policy=legacy-contig`) to see if fragmentation stops growing.

alex: Will test now on the on-prem box and run the long_ctx suite overnight. I'll report numbers tomorrow.

maria_dev: Parallel experiment: I'll run a Dedicated replica with same config but force `kernel-select.policy=v2.3-contig` to see if we can reproduce hosted -> dedicated diff. If we see same growth, then it's definitely kernel heuristics + allocator interaction.

kv-profiler-bot: scheduled job `long_ctx_recheck/176820` queued (ETA 12h).

jordan_pm: Good. Once repro steps are solid, we should bake a guard in the console: if frag_ratio > 0.35 AND compaction_runs==0, flip to safe defaults automatically for Private images (opt-in by tenant). Could avoid incidents. :+1:

chris_sre: Agree. Also add a regression test to perf CI: run 20k token incremental growth and assert frag_ratio < 0.3 after 2 hours.

alex: Quick note: on the on-prem test I saw a tiny perf regression in end-to-end latency after enabling compaction (~3-4% p50). But unit cost/tokens improved due to fewer page faults. We'll weigh tradeoffs.

maria_dev: Thanks — if you can drop the CI reproducer + config diff in the thread I'll pick it up. Also open a small onprem patch to default to `kv.compact_on_eviction=true` in the private image until allocator is replaced.

alex: Uploaded repro + config to `gs://internal-redwood/kv-repro/176820/` and created a short runbook in the ticket RED-3421.

chris_sre: Nice work. Ping me if the overnight run shows >10k page_faults again.

alex: Will do. Thanks all. :rocket:
